money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency is the Central African CFA Franc (XAF). Cameroon, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea also use the XAF. Very few ATMs are available in Bangui. Bangui has several Western Union offices, but only a few banks. Most hotels, supermarkets and restaurants catering to foreigners only accept cash. Bangui is the only city where you can change money. You can usually convert euros or US dollars into local currency. Keep alert when changing money through official or unofficial change agents.

laws.rule: Local law requires you to always carry your passport. Always carry proof of identity. Police might detain or fine you if you can't show them identity documents.
laws.heading: Proof of identity

laws.rule: Unauthorised photography is illegal. Don't take photos of: military zones military assets military or police personnel government buildings mining leases If you do, police may confiscate your camera, fine you and detain you. You need a government permit to take photos. The government will not grant permits for strategic sites such as: the airport military buildings the Presidential Palace It's not permitted to take photographs the authorities think damage the country’s image (for example, of street children and people with disabilities).
laws.heading: Photography

laws.rule: A licence is necessary to buy or sell gems. There are heavy penalties for illegally exporting precious gems. It's only legal to purchase diamonds or precious stones through government-authorised agents.
laws.heading: Gem licences

laws.rule: While same-sex relationships are not illegal, they are not widely accepted in Central African society. LGBTQIA+ travellers may face arrest for public displays of affection.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ information

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: FCDO's laws and cultural differences section for Central African Republic has no customs or etiquette guidance. National tourism and government sites were searched on 2026-11-01; none found. Ask locally. Photography anywhere in the country needs authorisation: the Ministry of Tourism and Handicrafts (Rond-point de la Paix, Bangui) issues it for private use, Centrafrique Presse for professional use. Never photograph government, military or police sites, the presidential palace, airports, power stations or people in uniform.
